title_en: Notice of the Ministry of Public Security, the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission, the Supreme People's Court, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Justice, the National Health Commission, the All-China Women's Federation, and the Office of the State Council Working Committee on Women and Children on Issuing the Opinions on Strengthening the Implementation of the Domestic Violence Warning System

Ministry of Public Security  Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission  Supreme People's Court  Ministry of Education

Ministry of Civil Affairs  Ministry of Justice  National Health Commission  All-China Women's Federation

Office of the State Council Working Committee on Women and Children

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Strengthening the Implementation of the Domestic Violence Admonishment System

Public Security Communication [2024] No. 34

The Public Security Departments (Bureaus), Party Political and Legal Affairs Committees, Higher People's Courts, Education Departments (Bureaus), Civil Affairs Departments (Bureaus), Justice Departments (Bureaus), Health Commissions, Women's Federations, and Women and Children Working Committee Offices of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Public Security Bureau, Party Political and Legal Affairs Committee of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; the Education Bureau, Civil Affairs Bureau, Justice Bureau, Health Commission, Women's Federation, and Women and Children Working Committee Office of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In order to thoroughly implement General Secretary Xi Jinping's important directives on women's and children's work and on family, family education, and family values; to implement the guiding principles of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Second and Third Plenary Sessions of the 20th Central Committee; to fully leverage the role of the domestic violence admonishment system; to actively intervene in and resolve family and marital disputes; to prevent and stop domestic violence; and to better maintain family harmony and social stability, in accordance with the Anti-Domestic Violence Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and regulations, the Ministry of Public Security, the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission, the Supreme People's Court, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Justice, the National Health Commission, the All-China Women's Federation, and the Office of the State Council Working Committee on Women and Children have formulated the Opinions on Strengthening the Implementation of the Domestic Violence Admonishment System, which are hereby issued to you for careful implementation. Problems encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported separately to the Ministry of Public Security, the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission, the Supreme People's Court, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Justice, the National Health Commission, the All-China Women's Federation, and the Office of the State Council Working Committee on Women and Children.

December 6, 2024

Opinions on Strengthening the Implementation of the Domestic Violence Admonishment System

In order to fully leverage the role of the domestic violence admonishment system, actively intervene in and resolve family and marital disputes, effectively prevent and stop domestic violence, protect the legitimate rights and interests of family members according to law, maintain equal, harmonious, and civilized family relationships, and promote family harmony and social stability, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Anti-Domestic Violence Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant laws and regulations, and in light of the actual work on anti-domestic violence.

I. For the purposes of these Opinions, "admonishment" refers to an administrative guidance act whereby public security organs issue a written warning and exhortation to a perpetrator who commits domestic violence of a minor nature and is not subject to public security penalties according to law, and, together with relevant departments and grassroots organizations, supervise the perpetrator to desist from committing domestic violence.

II. After receiving a report of domestic violence, the public security organ shall promptly dispatch police, stop the domestic violence, investigate and collect evidence in accordance with relevant regulations, and determine the facts of the domestic violence according to law.

III. Public security organs determining the facts of domestic violence shall meet the following basic evidentiary conditions:

(1) If the perpetrator has no objection to committing the domestic violence, a statement from the perpetrator, a statement from the victim, or testimony from a witness is required;

(2) If the perpetrator denies committing the domestic violence, a statement from the victim or testimony from a witness, plus one other type of supplementary evidence, is required.

IV. Types of supplementary evidence that public security organs may apply when determining the facts of domestic violence include:

(1) Audio-visual materials recording the process of the domestic violence;

(2) Electronic data such as telephone recordings, text messages, instant messaging communications, and emails related to the domestic violence;

(3) Testimony from relatives, friends, neighbors, and other witnesses, as well as testimony from the minor children of the parties that is appropriate for their age and intelligence;

(4) Letters of repentance or guarantees previously issued by the perpetrator;

(5) Forensic injury assessment opinions;

(6) Medical treatment records from medical institutions;

(7) Records of domestic violence complaints, reports, or requests for assistance received by relevant departments or units;

(8) Other evidence capable of proving that the victim suffered domestic violence.

V. If the circumstances of domestic violence are minor and no public security penalty is imposed according to law, the public security organ may give the perpetrator a criticism education or issue an Admonishment Letter.

VI. Where the facts of domestic violence have been verified, the circumstances are minor, and any of the following circumstances exist, an Admonishment Letter shall generally be issued:

(1) The perpetrator has previously received criticism education from a public security organ for committing domestic violence;

(2) The domestic violence is committed against a minor, an elderly person, a person with a disability, a pregnant or breastfeeding woman, or a person with a serious illness;

(3) The domestic violence is committed in a public place;

(4) The victim requests the issuance;

(5) Other circumstances where an Admonishment Letter should be issued according to law.

If the perpetrator admits to committing the domestic violence but argues that the victim was at fault, this does not affect the public security organ's issuance of the Admonishment Letter according to law.

VII. If the circumstances of domestic violence are extremely minor, or if the circumstances are minor and the perpetrator obtains the victim's forgiveness, the public security organ may give the perpetrator a criticism education.

Where a criticism education is given to the perpetrator, a record shall be made in the relevant case reporting information system for future reference.

VIII. If the perpetrator has no objection to committing the domestic violence, or if, despite objection, the facts of the domestic violence are clear, the public security organ may decide on the spot to give a criticism education or issue an Admonishment Letter, and shall use equipment such as body-worn cameras to record audio and video for future reference. If further verification is needed, a decision shall be made within 72 hours after accepting the report.

IX. The content of the Admonishment Letter shall include the identity information of the perpetrator and the victim and their relationship, a factual statement of the domestic violence, the evidence found, relevant legal provisions, the prohibition against the perpetrator committing domestic violence, and the legal consequences of committing domestic violence again. The Admonishment Letter shall be made in triplicate: one copy to the perpetrator, one copy to the victim, and one copy kept on file by the public security organ. The format of the Admonishment Letter shall be uniformly formulated by the Ministry of Public Security.

The public security organ shall promptly enter the Admonishment Letter and related archival information into the law enforcement case handling information system.

X. When serving the Admonishment Letter, the public security organ shall read the admonishment content to the perpetrator in person, and the perpetrator shall sign and affix their fingerprint. If the perpetrator refuses to sign for receipt of the Admonishment Letter without legitimate reason, the police officer shall note the circumstances and record the reading and service process by audio and video for future reference; the service shall then be deemed completed.

XI. The public security organ shall promptly notify the local residents' committee, villagers' committee, women's federation, and township (subdistrict) comprehensive management center of the admonishment situation.

When implementing the admonishment, staff from the local residents' committee, villagers' committee, women's federation, and child welfare officers may be notified to be present.

XII. Public security police stations shall conduct visitation and supervision of perpetrators and victims who have received Admonishment Letters.

Within seven days after serving the Admonishment Letter, the public security police station shall conduct an initial visitation of the perpetrator and victim to supervise the perpetrator's desistance from committing domestic violence again. If no further domestic violence is found during the initial visitation, a visitation shall be conducted every three months. If no further domestic violence by the perpetrator is found in three consecutive visitations, visitations shall cease.

Visitations may be conducted jointly with the residents' committee or villagers' committee. The residents' committee or villagers' committee shall cooperate with the public security police station in joint visitations, or conduct visitations independently, and shall strengthen the work of resolving family disputes. The grassroots women's federation shall assist and cooperate in carrying out relevant work.

If a visitation finds that the perpetrator has committed domestic violence again, legal liability shall be pursued according to law.

XIII. Education administrative, health, and civil affairs departments shall strengthen professional training on anti-domestic violence, and shall supervise and guide schools, kindergartens, medical institutions, residents' committees, villagers' committees, social work service organizations, relief management institutions, welfare institutions, and child protection agencies and their staff to implement the mandatory reporting system. When discovering in their work that a person with no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct is suffering or is suspected of suffering domestic violence, they shall promptly report the matter to the public security organ.

XIV. The Admonishment Letter may serve as a written certificate for a domestic violence victim to voluntarily apply for shelter at a temporary shelter, and the temporary shelter shall provide the victim with temporary living assistance.

For persons with no capacity for civil conduct or persons with limited capacity for civil conduct who have suffered serious physical harm from domestic violence, face threats to their personal safety, or are in a dangerous state such as being unattended, the public security organ shall notify and assist the civil affairs department in placing them in a temporary shelter, relief management institution, welfare institution, or child protection agency.

XV. When handling domestic violence according to law, the public security organ shall proactively inform the victim that they may apply to the people's court for a personal safety protection order. If a party is a person with no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, or is unable to apply for a personal safety protection order due to coercion, intimidation, or other reasons, the application may be made on their behalf.

XVI. When hearing cases involving domestic violence, the people's court may determine the facts of domestic violence based on evidence such as the public security organ's dispatch records, the Admonishment Letter, and the forensic injury assessment opinion.

In cases such as divorce, where a party merely claims the existence of domestic violence facts on the grounds that the public security organ has issued an Admonishment Letter, the people's court shall conduct a comprehensive determination of whether such facts exist according to law.

XVII. A domestic violence victim may, based on the Admonishment Letter, apply to a legal aid institution for legal aid such as legal consultation and drafting of legal documents. The legal aid institution shall, according to law and regulations, provide legal aid to the domestic violence victim.

XVIII. In the process of handling domestic violence cases, if the public security organ finds that the parents or other guardians of a minor have improperly educated the minor or infringed upon the minor's legitimate rights and interests, it may order them to receive family education guidance.

The education administrative department shall guide and supervise schools and kindergartens to conduct education on family virtues and anti-domestic violence for the parents or other guardians of students and children. When necessary, primary and secondary schools and kindergartens shall cooperate with public security organs to supervise the parents or other guardians of students or children who have committed domestic violence to receive family education guidance. Primary and secondary schools and kindergartens with the necessary conditions shall, under the guidance of the education administrative department, provide support for family education guidance service sites to carry out public welfare family education guidance service activities.

XIX. The women's federation, residents' committee, and villagers' committee shall, based on the notification from the public security organ regarding the admonishment, conduct legal education for the perpetrator who committed domestic violence, and when necessary, may provide psychological counseling to both the perpetrator and the victim.

Education administrative and civil affairs departments shall guide schools, social work service organizations, and other relevant units to conduct psychological problem assessment and counseling, psychological crisis intervention, and consultation for minor victims of domestic violence or minors who have witnessed domestic violence. The health department shall guide medical institutions in carrying out psychological crisis intervention and psychological treatment for minors.

XX. Where domestic violence involves any of the following circumstances, constituting a violation of public security administration or suspected criminal offenses, legal liability of the perpetrator shall be pursued according to law, and incrimination and administrative or criminal penalties shall not be replaced by admonishment:

(1) The perpetrator refuses to stop the violence after being stopped on the spot by the police;

(2) The perpetrator commits domestic violence again during mediation;

(3) The perpetrator, after being admonished or penalized by the public security organ, does not repent and commits domestic violence again;

(4) The perpetrator commits domestic violence multiple times;

(5) Other circumstances where legal liability should be pursued.

XXI. Public security organs shall strengthen statistics on domestic violence police incidents, conduct classified statistics on incidents involving entities subject to the mandatory reporting obligation, and compile statistics on the results of handling according to the categories of criticism education, issuance of Admonishment Letters, imposition of administrative penalties, and pursuit of criminal liability.

XXII. The institution responsible for women's and children's work of the people's government at or above the county level shall strengthen the overall planning for the implementation of the domestic violence admonishment system, organize, coordinate, guide, and supervise relevant departments to strengthen publicity and training, keep abreast of the situation, promote information exchange, resource sharing, and coordination and linkage, and utilize the regular consultation mechanism on anti-domestic violence work to provide safeguards for the effective linkage between admonishment and other anti-domestic violence systems.

XXIII. Anti-domestic violence work shall protect the privacy of the parties involved. Departments, organizations, and personnel handling domestic violence cases and incidents shall have a duty of confidentiality regarding the information and privacy of the parties, witnesses, whistleblowers, and other relevant persons they become aware of.

XXIV. Violent acts committed between persons who live together but are not family members shall be handled by reference to these Opinions. "Persons who live together but are not family members" generally includes a cohabiting daughter-in-law, son-in-law, parents-in-law, as well as other persons with relationships of guardianship, support, foster care, or cohabitation.

Excerpts of Relevant Laws:

Anti-Domestic Violence Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 2: For the purposes of this Law, "domestic violence" refers to physical, psychological, and other forms of harm inflicted among family members through means such as beating, binding, mutilation, restriction of personal freedom, and recurrent verbal abuse and intimidation.

Article 3: Family members shall assist each other, care for each other, live in harmony, and fulfill family obligations.

Opposing domestic violence is the common responsibility of the state, society, and every family.

The state prohibits all forms of domestic violence.

Article 16: If the circumstances of domestic violence are minor and no public security penalty is imposed according to law, the public security organ shall give the perpetrator a criticism education or issue an Admonishment Letter.

Article 17: The public security organ shall serve the Admonishment Letter to the perpetrator and the victim and notify the residents' committee and the villagers' committee.

The residents' committee, villagers' committee, and public security police station shall conduct visitation and supervision of the perpetrator and victim who have received the Admonishment Letter, and supervise the perpetrator to desist from committing domestic violence again.

Article 33: If a perpetrator commits domestic violence, constituting a violation of public security administration, a public security penalty shall be imposed according to law; if it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law.

Article 37: Violent acts committed between persons who live together but are not family members shall be handled by reference to this Law.

Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 234: Whoever intentionally injures the body of another person shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance.

Whoever commits the crime in the preceding paragraph, causing serious injury to another person, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years; if death or serious disability is caused by particularly cruel means, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death. Where this Law provides otherwise, such provisions shall apply.

Article 260: Whoever maltreats a family member, if the circumstances are flagrant, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years, criminal detention, or public surveillance.

Whoever commits the crime in the preceding paragraph, causing serious injury or death to the victim, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than two years but not more than seven years.
